title: Title V Major Source — NOx
description: Facilities with a potential to emit ≥100 tons/yr (90.7 t) of any criteria pollutant require a Title V Operating Permit. In Serious ozone nonattainment areas the NOx threshold drops to 50 tons/yr (45.4 t). Emergency engines are evaluated on a 500 h/yr potential-to-emit basis.
source: Clean Air Act Title V, 42 U.S.C. § 7661; 40 CFR 70.2 (major source, potential to emit)
citation: EPA, 'Who Has to Obtain a Title V Permit?' (2025); 40 CFR Part 70; EPA emergency-engine PTE convention (500 h/yr)

title: Title V Major Source — PM2.5
description: Facilities with a potential to emit ≥100 tons/yr (90.7 t) of PM2.5 require a Title V Operating Permit (500 h/yr PTE basis for emergency engines).
source: Clean Air Act Title V, 42 U.S.C. § 7661; 40 CFR 70.2
citation: 40 CFR Part 70; EPA Title V applicability guidance

title: Hazardous Air Pollutant (HAP) Major Source
description: Facilities with a potential to emit ≥10 tons/yr (9.07 t) of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/yr (22.7 t) combined HAPs are major sources under CAA Section 112. Formaldehyde from the generator fleet is estimated with AP-42 factors by engine type (500 h/yr PTE basis for emergency engines).
source: Clean Air Act Section 112(a)(1), 42 U.S.C. § 7412
citation: EPA, 'Summary of the Clean Air Act' — Section 112; 40 CFR Part 63; EPA AP-42 Tables 3.1-3 (gas turbines), 3.4-3 (large stationary diesel)

title: Generator Non-Emergency Runtime Limit
description: EPA limits non-emergency operation of stationary diesel generators to 100 hours per year under RICE NESHAP (40 CFR Part 63, Subpart ZZZZ).
source: 40 CFR Part 63, Subpart ZZZZ (RICE NESHAP)
citation: EPA, 'Stationary RICE NESHAP'; EPA Clean Air Act Resources for Data Centers (Dec 2025)

title: EPA GHG Reporting Program Threshold
description: Facilities emitting ≥25,000 metric tons CO2e/yr must report under EPA's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (40 CFR Part 98).
source: 40 CFR Part 98 — Mandatory GHG Reporting
citation: EPA GHG Reporting Program; Encino Environmental (2025)

title: NAAQS PM2.5 Annual Standard
description: Primary annual PM2.5 standard was lowered to 9.0 µg/m³ in Feb 2024. Note: EPA requested vacatur of this rule in Nov 2025; the prior standard of 12.0 µg/m³ may be reinstated. Both values are flagged.
source: 40 CFR Part 50 — NAAQS for PM
citation: EPA final rule Feb 7 2024 (89 FR 16202); EPA reconsideration announced Mar 12 2025; Harvard EELP Tracker

title: WHO Noise Guideline — Sustained Exposure
description: WHO states sustained exposure above 70 dBA risks hearing damage. Many local ordinances adopt this or stricter limits (typically 55-65 dBA at residential boundary).
source: WHO Guidelines for Community Noise (1999); WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region (2018)
citation: WHO, 'Guidelines for Community Noise,' Table 4.1; referenced in EPA Noise Control Act

title: PUE Benchmark (ISO 30134-2)
description: Power Usage Effectiveness per ISO 30134-2. Industry average is 1.58; hyperscalers achieve 1.1-1.2. Values above 1.6 indicate significant cooling/distribution inefficiency.
source: ISO 30134-2:2016; The Green Grid
citation: AWS 2024 Sustainability Report (PUE 1.15 global); IDC 2025 (on-premises avg 1.63)

title: WUE Benchmark (The Green Grid)
description: Water Usage Effectiveness. Industry average 1.8 L/kWh. AWS reports 0.15 globally (2024). Values above 2.5 indicate excessive water consumption.
source: The Green Grid; ISO 30134
citation: EESI (2025); AWS 2024 Sustainability Report (0.15 L/kWh); LBNL US DC Energy Report (2024)

title: WRI Aqueduct Water Stress
description: World Resources Institute water stress score. Score ≥3 = High, ≥4 = Extremely High. 32% of US data centers are in high or extremely high stress areas.
source: WRI Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas
citation: Ceres, 'Drained by Data' (2025); WRI Aqueduct 4.0

title: Grid Reserve Margin (NERC/PJM)
description: NERC and PJM target a minimum 15% planning reserve margin to ensure grid reliability. Data center load that pushes reserve below this level creates systemic risk.
source: NERC Reliability Standards; PJM planning criteria
citation: JLARC 2024 (Virginia); PJM 2025 Capacity Auction results

title: Transmission Utilization
description: Transmission line loading above 85% of rated capacity reduces N-1 contingency margins and increases outage risk.
source: PJM Reliability Standards; NERC TPL Standards
citation: JLARC 2024; IEA Energy and AI (2025) — '20% of planned DCs could face grid connection delays'

title: Environmental Justice Screening
description: EPA EJScreen identifies communities with disproportionate environmental and health burdens. Scores above the 80th percentile indicate high concern for cumulative impacts.
source: EPA EJScreen; CDC Social Vulnerability Index
citation: EPA, 'EJScreen: Environmental Justice Screening Tool'; CDC/ATSDR SVI

title: Monetized Health Damages
description: EPA benefit-per-ton values and BenMAP-CE concentration-response functions estimate health costs from air pollution using Value of Statistical Life ($11.6M, 2024). Health damages above $1M/yr indicate significant community burden.
source: EPA benefit-per-ton TSD (June 2024); EPA VSL ($11.6M, 2024)
citation: EPA, 'Technical Support Document: Estimating the Benefit per Ton of Reducing Directly-Emitted PM2.5, PM2.5 Precursors and Ozone Precursors from 21 Sectors' (June 2024); Pope et al. ACS Cohort Study

title: Net Community Fiscal Impact
description: Total community value accounts for tax revenue, jobs, and infrastructure benefits minus incentives, public costs, health damages, environmental damage, and agricultural losses. Negative values mean costs exceed benefits.
source: Brookings Institution CBA Framework (Jan 2026); NAACP DC CBA Template
citation: Brookings, 'Community Benefits from Data Centers' (2026); JLARC 2024 (Virginia cost study)

title: Ratepayer Cost Shift
description: Infrastructure costs socialized to residential ratepayers. Virginia experience shows data center growth contributing $8-10/month bill increases. Significant community opposition trigger.
source: Dominion Energy 2025 IRP; PJM Market Monitor
citation: Belfer Center (2025); AAF (2026) — Dominion proposed $8.51/month increase; PJM Market Monitor: '$16.6B capacity market revenue increase attributed to DC load'

title: Food Supply Displacement
description: When a data center displaces more than 2% of local food supply, it can trigger price impacts and food security concerns, especially in agricultural regions.
source: Framework analysis; USDA food security methodology
citation: USDA Economic Research Service; Framework Doc benchmarks

title: Hardware Reuse/Recycle Rate
description: Best practice targets 80%+ reuse/recycle with <5% to landfill. Microsoft Amsterdam Circular Center achieves 83% reuse. Global e-waste recycling rate is only 22%.
source: UN Global E-Waste Monitor (2024); Microsoft Circular Economy Program
citation: Microsoft, '83% reuse, 17% recycle at Amsterdam Circular Center'; UN GEWR 2024 (22.3% global recycling)

title: Aquifer Depletion Risk
description: When facility water withdrawal exceeds 5% of aquifer recharge rate, depletion risk becomes significant. Above 10%, the withdrawal is unsustainable long-term and may conflict with existing water rights.
source: USGS Groundwater Depletion Studies; State water management frameworks
citation: USGS Circular 1323 'Groundwater Depletion in the United States'; ADWR (Arizona), ODNR (Ohio) groundwater management rules

title: Basin Water Stress Contribution
description: Facility contribution to total basin water stress. When a single facility uses more than 1% of basin available water, it becomes a material contributor to regional water stress.
source: WRI Aqueduct methodology; EPA Water Quality Standards framework
citation: WRI Aqueduct 4.0; Ceres 'Drained by Data' (2025)

title: Local Temperature Impact
description: Data center waste heat contributes to urban heat island effect. IPCC identifies +1.5°C as a concern threshold for local warming impacts on health and cooling demand.
source: IPCC AR6; California EPA UHI methodology
citation: IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 10; Framework Doc UHI analysis
